title: How Do People Rate Cities?

source.name: Diễn đạt lại từ ý tưởng của một đoạn đọc về khảo sát City Brands Index trong sách Complete IELTS Bands 4–5 (Cambridge University Press)
source.license: Văn bản do web viết lại hoàn toàn bằng lời khác; chỉ giữ thông tin; câu hỏi và ghi chú soạn riêng
source.note: Bản diễn đạt lại; không phải trích nguyên văn.

paras: Which city would you most like to live in? Many websites rank cities, and most of them rely on hard data such as prices, jobs and crime figures that officials collect.

The City Brands Index takes a different route. It treats a city like a product, for example a brand of trainers, and asks ordinary people to give it a score. The surprising part is that the people who answer have often never been there. They judge a city by what they have picked up from the news, magazines and television.

Every year, around ten thousand people in twenty countries complete an online questionnaire about fifty cities. They give marks for things such as the economy, education, the environment, culture, the weather and the people who live there.

Why does this matter? Someone planning to move, study or take a holiday can see how a city looks from the outside. City governments can learn why visitors and companies choose to come, or stay away, and then decide what to improve.

questions.q: What makes the City Brands Index different from most other city rankings?
options: It relies on public opinion rather than on official statistics
It only compares cities that attract very large numbers of tourists
It uses prices and crime figures that city officials have collected
It asks city governments to give marks to their own cities
questions.explain: Đoạn 1–2: các bảng xếp hạng khác dựa vào “hard data … that officials collect”; City Brands Index “asks ordinary people to give it a score” ≈ dựa vào ý kiến công chúng, không dựa vào số liệu chính thức.

questions.q: In paragraph 2, why does the writer mention a brand of trainers?
options: To prove that shoes are the most popular product people think about in the survey
To suggest that living in a big city is as expensive as buying a pair of sports shoes
To explain that the people who answer the questionnaire are all keen athletes
To show that the index treats a city in the way a company treats something it sells
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: “It treats a city like a product, for example a brand of trainers” → ví dụ để cho thấy thành phố được xem như một thương hiệu/sản phẩm.

questions.q: What is surprising about many of the people who take part in the survey?
options: They live in the cities they are asked to score
They are experts in business and economics
They work for the city governments
They have never visited the places they are judging
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: “The surprising part is that the people who answer have often never been there.”

questions.q: Which of these is NOT something the participants give marks for?
options: The people who live there
The standard of education
The quality of the local sports teams
The state of the natural environment
questions.explain: Đoạn 3 liệt kê: economy, education, environment, culture, weather, people. Không có sports teams.

questions.q: How could a city government use the results?
options: To decide how much money visitors should be charged for tickets and hotel rooms
To understand what attracts or puts off visitors and companies, and then plan improvements
To count how many people live in each city so that taxes can be collected
To compare its own crime figures with the figures from other countries
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: chính quyền thành phố “can learn why visitors and companies choose to come, or stay away, and then decide what to improve”.

questions.q: Participants fill in the questionnaire in person in the cities they are rating.
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: họ “complete an online questionnaire”, và đoạn 2 cho biết nhiều người chưa từng đến thành phố đó.

questions.q: Most of the people who answer the survey are under thirty years old.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói khoảng mười nghìn người ở hai mươi nước; không nói về độ tuổi.
